_meta.title: rusti Feature Tracker
_meta.description: Tracks feature status for the rusti Rust coding agent

features.name: Project Setup & Baseline
features.description: Confirm cargo build, cargo test, ./init.sh, and --self-test all pass from a clean checkout
features.evidence: cargo build --release (2.6 MB), cargo test passes, --self-test passes

features.name: Core Agent Loop
features.description: System prompt â†’ user task â†’ LLM tool calls â†’ tool execution â†’ feedback loop terminates correctly
features.evidence: run_agent in ai_core/mod.rs, verified by --self-test (fake SSE server)

features.name: LLM Streaming & SSE
features.description: Streaming responses via reqwest SSE, JSON fragment accumulation for tool-call arguments
features.evidence:
chat_stream in ai_core/llm.rs, handles 

 and

features.name: Tool Implementations
features.description: read_file, write_file, edit_file, run_command, ask_user tools work correctly and report errors
features.evidence: ai_core/tools.rs, the original 5 tools; edit_file enforces a unique match, run_command is platform-aware. Extended by feat-021 (grep/glob/list_dir/multi_edit, ranged reads, timeout) and feat-023 (delete/move, background jobs, todo, delegate, permission gate, root guard) â€” 16 tools total

features.evidence: config.rs, interactive add when empty, EOF-safe prompts, profiles with default pointer

features.name: TUI Mode

features.evidence: src/tui/ module (mod/app/render/plain), main-screen (no alternate screen), diff rendering with RenderState, CSI 2026 for atomic frames, plain stream fallback for piped stdin

features.name: Self-Test
features.description: --self-test runs offline check with fake server, no network required
features.evidence: ai_core/mod.rs self_test(), fake SSE server with 2 requests, sync tool assertions, session tree checks

features.name: Session Persistence & Tree Branching
features.description: session.json with tree structure (id/parentId), active leaf, --tree browser (pi-style main-screen + diff rendering), --resume, pi-style branching
features.evidence: session.rs (Entry/Session), tree.rs (main-screen diff renderer + plain list), --tree/--resume in main.rs

features.name: Live LLM Integration
features.description: Tested against local LLM server (localhost:20128), model profiles with API key, streaming works end-to-end
features.evidence: model.json with mimo-v2.5-pro default, key persisted, streaming verified via curl and rusti CLI

features.name: TUI Experience: semantic status + spinner + editing + scrollback + slash commands
features.description: Semantic status symbols/colors (â ‹ working, âœ“ success, âœ— failure, âš  warn, â„¹ info, cyan â€º prompt), animated spinner, cursor editing + history recall, PageUp/PageDown scrollback, /use /resume /tree slash commands, input overflow window, user lines flush-left with dim number + cyan caret
features.evidence: tools.rs returns (bool,String); Event::ToolStart/ToolEnd/TaskEnd; Job enum (Task/Model/Resume/Tree); cursor/history/scroll fields in App; SPINNER frames in render.rs; colorize_row semantic colors; self-test green

features.name: Interrupt Key Model (pi-style)
features.description: Esc interrupts the running agent (cooperative AtomicBool checked between iterations and per stream chunk), Ctrl+C clears input, Ctrl+D exits when input empty; interrupted turns show 'âš  interrupted'; quit no longer waits for in-flight turn
features.evidence: cancel: Arc<AtomicBool> shared TUI<->agent; run_agent/chat_stream take &AtomicBool; self-test asserts pre-set flag returns Err("interrupted") before any network call

features.name: /reload: hot rebuild + relaunch
features.description: TUI slash command rebuilds rusti from its own source (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) into target/reload, runs a uniquely-named copy of the binary (never the built file itself, so cargo can always overwrite it despite Windows exe-locking), and relaunches: exec on Unix, wait-as-thin-wrapper on Windows (exiting after spawn would let the shell fight the child for console input). Preserves the session (saved first, then --resume), live model (--url/--key/--model, survives a mid-session /use), and visible transcript (reconstructed from session.json on the new process). Guarded to idle turns only; build failures leave the running session untouched. /model opens an arrow-key picker over saved profiles (active marked, starts selected) or switches by name.
features.evidence: tui/mod.rs: Job::Reload, stage_reload_exe/build_relaunch_args/render_history (latter two unit tested), Event::Reload handoff, cfg(unix) exec vs cfg(not(unix)) status(); app.rs: Exit::Reload return from ui_loop, /reload gated on app.done, /model + shared switch_model/list_models; fixed pre-existing job_tx/join deadlock on quit and a blocking stdin prompt under --tui --resume as prerequisites; ai_core: resumed session's system entry refreshed from SYSTEM_PROMPT each turn; verified: cargo build into target/reload + staged copy runs --self-test

features.name: Tool wall time
features.description: Every finished tool row carries its own wall time (âœ“ src/main.rs  450ms); Event::ToolEnd gained an ms field, measured around dispatch in run_agent and around the cargo build in /reload
features.evidence: ai_core::took unit-checked in --self-test; visible as 'âœ“ echo hi  15ms' in --self-test output

features.name: Ctrl+C twice to exit
features.description: First Ctrl+C clears the input and cancels a running turn, a second within 2s quits; status line shows 'press ctrl+c again to exit' in yellow while armed, any other key disarms. /quit added as the explicit equivalent
features.evidence: cargo build clean; App::armed drives the status line; /quit returns Exit::Quit from handle_command

features.name: Per-turn token/tps/wall stats
features.description: After each turn: 'Â· 142 tok Â· 38.4 tps Â· 6.2s', dim. Tokens come from the server's usage.completion_tokens when sent, else a chars/4 estimate marked with '~'; tps is over generation time only (clock starts at the first token) so tool waits don't dilute it
features.evidence: tui::tests::turn_stats_row_reports_tps_over_generation_time_only

features.name: reasoning_content thinking block
features.description: Thinking models' reasoning_content (or reasoning) deltas stream into a dim 'â”‚ ' block that closes when the answer or a tool call starts; never folded into content or sent back to the model. Plain mode writes it to stderr
features.evidence: --self-test fake SSE stream includes a reasoning_content delta; final content stays exactly 'done'

features.name: Slash-command menu
features.description: Typing a lone '/word' opens the command menu above the input: 5 rows visible, up/down walks the whole filtered list, Tab completes, Enter runs, Esc dismisses for that text, 'n/total' counter row when it overflows. Queued commands (/undo /commit /plan /test /export) are listed with 'Â· soon' and print a pointer to harness/open-work.md when run
features.evidence: tui::tests::slash_menu_filters_on_prefix_and_closes_once_args_start

features.name: Named sessions + /resume picker
features.description: --session NAME (or RUSTI_SESSION) stores a session at .rusti/sessions/NAME.json, the root session.json staying the unnamed default. /resume with no argument opens an arrow-driven picker (name, entries, relative age, latest user message); /resume 2 or /resume NAME skips it. Resuming replaces the on-screen transcript and recallable history via Event::Resumed
features.evidence: session::tests::info_reports_entry_count_and_latest_user_message; tests::task_arg_skips_flag_values; smoke: rusti --session smoke "..." wrote .rusti/sessions/smoke.json and answered

features.name: Active session name in status line
features.description: The status line's right slot reads '<session> Â· <model>' (prototype shows the name in its title bar); seeded from the session file's stem, updated by Event::SessionName on resume and rename
features.evidence: cargo build clean; name_of() covered by session::tests; visible as 'two Â· Qwen/...' when launched with --session two

features.name: /rename <new-name>
features.description: Renames the active session's file to .rusti/sessions/<name>.json: ASCII letters/digits/._- up to 40 chars, refuses a taken name or the current one, moves the file when it exists (an unsaved session just repoints), prints 'â„¹ renamed old â†’ new'. /reload's relaunch argv now carries the live session name so a rename survives a hot rebuild. /session list|switch listed in the menu as 'Â· soon'
features.evidence: tui::tests::rename_moves_the_session_file_and_refuses_bad_or_taken_names; session::tests covers valid_name; tui::tests::relaunch_args_replace_model_and_dedupe_resume asserts the --session pair is replaced

features.name: Native Search & Edit Tools
features.description: grep (ripgrep when installed, std substring fallback), glob (rg --files or std walk + own matcher), list_dir (depth, skip list), read_file offset/limit with line numbers, multi_edit all-or-nothing, run_command timeout_secs (default 120, kill at deadline)
features.evidence: --self-test asserts glob_match cases, list_dir/glob/grep on the repo, ranged read, multi_edit atomicity, 1s timeout kills ping/sleep; passes with rg on PATH and with PATH=System32 (fallback path)

features.name: Iteration Cap & Project Instructions
features.description: MAX_ITERS 10 -> 50, overridable with --max-iters N / RUSTI_MAX_ITERS; system prompt appends AGENTS.md (fallback RUSTI.md, CLAUDE.md) from cwd, re-read every turn so edits are live, capped at 20k chars
features.evidence: --self-test: set_max_iters floor, instructions_from precedence (AGENTS.md > RUSTI.md, blank file skipped), system_prompt starts with SYSTEM_PROMPT

features.name: Agent Safety & Workflow Tools
features.description: Permission gate on write/edit/multi_edit/run_command/run_background/delete/move via Event::Ask (y / n / a=always for that tool), --yolo or RUSTI_YOLO=1 skips; project-root guard on all write paths (canonicalized deepest-existing ancestor, refuses ../ and absolute-outside); delete_file, move_file; run_background + job_output + job_stop (taskkill /T on Windows); todo list tool rendered to the transcript; delegate(task) runs a one-level sub-agent in its own .rusti/sessions/sub-*.json and returns only its report
features.evidence: --self-test: decide() y/yes/a/always/deny, guard() inside vs ../ vs temp dir, write refused outside root, move/delete roundtrip, background job running->stopped and echo job exited 0 with output, todo render; 0 warnings; cargo test 7 passed

features.name: TUI Markdown Rendering
features.description: Model prose renders markdown in the TUI: ATX headings, **bold**, `inline code`, - / * bullets as bullet glyphs, and fenced code blocks. No parser crate; markers are stripped and turned into style runs over the visible text so wrapping measures real columns. Fenced bodies are truncated, never reflowed. Tool rows, user queries, reasoning and stats keep their own styling
features.evidence: render.rs tests markdown_markers_become_styling_not_literal_characters and markdown_wrapping_measures_visible_text_not_markers; cargo test 12 passed

features.name: Alternate Screen TUI
features.description: The TUI runs on the terminal's alternate screen buffer (EnterAlternateScreen on start, LeaveAlternateScreen on exit, both quit and /reload paths) instead of the main screen. Launch paints a fresh canvas — no gap between the shell prompt and the bottom-pinned panel, no leftovers from previous runs; quit restores the primary buffer exactly, so shell history survives and the 'Come back again, boss' farewell lands right under the launch line. The earlier quit-time escape clears (ESC[2J/3J) are gone — 3J was eating the shell scrollback. Transcripts persist via session.json + /resume, not terminal scrollback.
features.evidence: src/tui/mod.rs run(): EnterAlternateScreen/cursor::Hide on start, cursor::Show/LeaveAlternateScreen before the Exit match; live-verified in PowerShell (no gap at launch, farewell under the prompt, scrollback intact); cargo test 13 passed; release build + --self-test OK

features.name: Multi-Tool-Call Message Integrity
features.description: A single assistant turn that emits several tool calls must send every tool result back; the message list must never contain a dangling tool call ("Tool result is missing for tool call ..." from the provider).
features.evidence: ai_core/mod.rs run_agent chains tool results (parent = previous tool entry) instead of fanning them under the assistant entry, so path_messages() keeps all of them on the active path. --self-test emits two tool calls and asserts 6 messages with msgs[3] and msgs[4] both role=tool. cargo test 13 passed; --self-test OK. Reported as: [CommandCode error: Tool result is missing for tool call call_00_7dueXDf20YUXmQlI48NA3107]

features.name: No Redundant Model-Switch Transcript Note
features.description: Switching models (/use, /model) must not print a note into the transcript; the bottom status line already shows <session> . <model>.
features.evidence: Removed the Event::Text("  model switched to {model}") from the Job::Model arm in tui/mod.rs; the status line updates immediately via app.model (set synchronously in switch_model). cargo check clean, cargo test 13 passed.

features.name: Prompt-Token Tracking
features.description: Event::Usage carries prompt (context size sent) alongside completion tokens; read from usage.prompt_tokens, estimated from the request body length when the server omits it (est flag set). The per-turn stats row ends with '· ctx 4.3k' (last call's prompt size). Prerequisite for context compaction, cost tracking, and a context-% footer.
features.evidence: tui::tests::turn_stats_row_reports_tps_over_generation_time_only asserts the ctx suffix and ~ estimate marker; cargo test 13 passed; --self-test OK (also fixed its stale 5-entries-on-disk assertion left over from feat-026).

features.name: Context Compaction
features.description: When the last request's prompt_tokens exceed CONTEXT_LIMIT (default 100k; --context N / RUSTI_CONTEXT), run_agent summarizes the active path minus its last ~8 entries with one LLM call, then branches system -> summary(user) -> copies of the tail. The tail cut snaps to a non-tool entry so no tool result dangles. Old entries stay in the tree (pi-style, nothing lost); the transcript shows '⟳ compacting context: N messages → summary'.
features.evidence: --self-test asserts compact_cut on short/no-system/14-entry/tool-boundary/tools-only paths and the set_context_limit floor; cargo test 13 passed; --self-test OK. Not yet exercised against a live model past 100k tokens.

features.name: Retry with Backoff
features.description: chat_stream retries connection failures and HTTP 408/429/5xx up to 3 times with 1s/2s/4s backoff (cancel-aware sleep), emitting '⚠ <err> — retry n/3 in Xs' to the transcript. Retries cover only the connect+status phase; once content has streamed the error surfaces as before so output is never duplicated. Other 4xx fail immediately.
features.evidence: --self-test fake server answers 503 on the first connection and the run still completes (RETRY_BASE_MS shrunk to 10ms); retryable() asserted for 503/429 vs 400/401. cargo test 13 passed; --self-test OK.

features.name: Tool Output Visibility (failures)
features.description: Event::ToolEnd carries the tool's output when it failed; every renderer (TUI, plain pipe, CLI stderr) prints the last 8 non-empty lines under the ✗ line as dim '  · ' rows, with a '… N more lines' header when truncated. Successful tools stay one line. No expand toggle yet.
features.evidence: --self-test asserts fail_tail on empty / CRLF+blank / 10-line inputs; cargo test 13 passed; --self-test OK.

features.name: /tree picker in the TUI
features.description: /tree opens the same panel picker as /resume and /model over the session's user/assistant entries (indented, active leaf marked ◀, cursor starts there). Enter sends Job::Select: the leaf moves pi-style (user entry -> its parent, text prefilled in the input for editing; assistant entry -> continue right after it), the session is saved, and the transcript is rebuilt via Event::Resumed. Replaces the old text dump. The '/undo' slash-command stub is removed: conversation undo is this; file undo stays in open-work.
features.evidence: tui::tests::selecting_a_user_entry_branches_at_its_parent_and_offers_its_text covers rows filtering, the ◀ mark, and both select semantics through render_history; cargo test 14 passed; --self-test OK. Interactive picker flow not driven by a test.

features.name: File Undo (/undo)
features.description: write_file/edit_file/multi_edit/delete_file/move_file snapshot each path's bytes (or absence) once per turn before touching it; run_agent clears the frame at depth 0 so a delegate sub-run belongs to the same turn. /undo restores those files in reverse order ('↶ restored X' / '↶ removed Y'), then rewinds the conversation to before the last user message via branch_at (shared with the /tree picker), prefilling that message for editing. One level only; refused while a task is running.
features.evidence: --self-test: two edits + one new file in a turn, undo_turn() returns ['removed _undo_b.txt', 'restored _undo_a.txt'], original bytes back, second undo empty. cargo test 14 passed; --self-test OK. /undo not driven interactively.

features.name: CLI --help and --version
features.description: --help / -h prints a one-screen reference (flags, env vars, slash commands, ! prefix) and exits; --version / -V prints CARGO_PKG_VERSION. Both are checked before every other argument so they work without a configured model. --json NDJSON output stays in open-work.
features.evidence: `rusti --version` prints 'rusti 0.1.0'; `rusti --help` prints the reference. cargo test 15 passed; --self-test OK.

features.name: Git awareness and /commit
features.description: system_prompt() appends a '# Git' section (branch + `git status --short`, truncated to 2k, 'working tree clean' when empty) and is rewritten every turn, so the model always sees the current tree. Event::Git carries the branch to the TUI status line, emitted before the first frame and after every job. /commit is a prompt macro that tells the model to review, stage and commit with a reasoned message (no push); it is refused while a task runs.
features.evidence: --self-test asserts git_context().is_some() == git_branch().is_some() and that the prompt carries '# Git\nbranch: ' inside a work tree. cargo test 15 passed. Verified live 2026-09-13 against cmc/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash: asked for the branch and tree state with tools forbidden, the model answered 'master' plus both dirty paths from context alone. /commit itself still not driven.

features.name: Bash mode (! prefix)
features.description: '!cmd' in the TUI runs cmd through tools::run_command on the agent thread and renders it as a tool line ('$ cmd') with its output shown on success as well as failure; the result is appended to the session as a user entry ('I ran `cmd` myself: …') so the model sees it next turn. Refused while a task is running; the raw '!cmd' goes into input history.
features.evidence: Compiles and routes through the existing ToolStart/ToolEnd path; cargo test 15 passed; --self-test OK. Not driven interactively.

features.name: Context and token footer
features.description: app::footer_right composes the status line's right side from the parts that exist: session · model · ⎇ branch · N tok (session total) · ctx N% (last prompt size against the --context limit). Session totals reset when /resume loads another session.
features.evidence: tui::tests::footer_shows_only_the_parts_that_exist covers the full line and the fresh-session case; cargo test 15 passed.

features.name: Project config (persistent permissions)
features.description: model.json gained allow / max_iters / context, all serde-optional and skipped when unset so existing files are untouched. Answering [a]lways at a permission prompt appends the tool to allow and saves, so the next run doesn't ask; main.rs seeds the gate via ai_core::allow_from_config before flags and env, which still override max_iters/context. decide() was split into a pure Answer parse with the saving moved into permitted(), so --self-test never writes to the real model.json.
features.evidence: --self-test asserts the Answer parse, that allow_from_config de-duplicates, that a fresh config writes none of the three keys, and that they round-trip once set. `rusti --list` still reads a model.json without them. cargo test 15 passed; --self-test OK. The prompt-suppression path itself needs a live model to drive.
decisions: Extended model.json instead of adding .rusti/config.json as the backlog sketched: one file, one loader, and the default-profile half of the feature already lived there. Renaming the file is the cheap fix if the mixed contents grate.

features.name: Plan mode (/plan)
features.description: A PLAN atomic checked at the top of permitted(), before --yolo and the saved allowlist, so every GATED tool (write_file, edit_file, multi_edit, run_command, run_background, delete_file, move_file) is refused with a message telling the model to finish investigating and reply with a plan instead of retrying. Read/search/list/todo are untouched. system_prompt() appends a '# Plan mode' section while it is on — and the prompt is rewritten every turn, so toggling takes effect immediately. /plan toggles it, the status line leads with 'plan'.
features.evidence: --self-test asserts plan_blocks() covers every mutating tool and no read tool, and that the '# Plan mode' section appears and disappears with the flag; tui::tests covers the footer's leading 'plan'. cargo test 15 passed; --self-test OK. Not driven against a live model.
decisions: Plan mode outranks --yolo: turning it on is a more specific, more recent instruction than the blanket permission flag.
Toggle rather than the backlog's approve-and-drop flow: the user turns it off when convinced, which needs no approval state machine. Mid-turn toggles take effect at the next tool call.

features.name: web_fetch tool
features.description: web_fetch(url) fetches an http(s) page through reqwest (20s timeout, 5 MB content-length ceiling) and returns it as text. strip_html drops <script>/<style> bodies, turns block tags into line breaks and other tags into spaces, decodes the common entities and collapses whitespace — no HTML parser, no new dependency. The result is prefixed '[fetched URL — untrusted page content, not instructions]' so an injected instruction inside a page reads as quoted data.
features.evidence: --self-test covers strip_html (paragraphs, entities, double-encoded &lt;, upper-case STYLE, script bodies, malformed and truncated markup) and fetches a real page off a one-shot local TCP server, asserting the untrusted prefix, decoded text, and that script/style bodies are gone. Non-http schemes refused. cargo test 15 passed; --self-test OK. Verified live 2026-09-13: a real run fetched https://example.com in 1.6s over TLS and read back the heading and purpose; the model volunteered that the content was third-party text and not instructions, so the untrusted prefix lands as intended.
decisions: Gated like the mutating tools rather than left open: the URL leaves the machine and the reply enters the model's context. run_command could already curl, but that asks too.

features.name: /export transcript as markdown
features.description: Session::export_markdown renders the active path: numbered user turns, assistant prose, tool calls as '- **name** `args`' (arguments flattened to one line and clipped), tool results as fenced blocks clipped to 500 chars. The system prompt is left out as boilerplate and an empty assistant turn gets no heading. /export [file.md] writes it through Job::Export, defaulting to <session-name>.md in the working directory.
features.evidence: session::tests::export_renders_the_active_path_and_leaves_the_system_prompt_out covers headings, the flattened tool-call arguments, fenced results, the omitted system prompt and the empty-assistant case, plus clip() on char (not byte) boundaries. cargo test 16 passed; --self-test OK. Not driven interactively.
decisions: Tool results are clipped to 500 chars: the export is for reading and issue-filing, and session.json remains the faithful record.

features.name: /session list|switch — dropped as redundant
features.description: The backlog item and its '· soon' menu stub are removed rather than implemented. /resume with no argument already opens a picker listing every saved session (names, entry counts, ages, last message) and switches to the chosen one; /resume <name> and /resume <n> already switch directly. /session would have been a second name for the same three behaviours. The /resume menu description now says so, so the capability is discoverable without a duplicate command.
features.evidence: Verified by reading tui/app.rs resume(): the arg branch resolves an index or a name to a path and sends Job::ResumePath; the no-arg branch builds the Session picker. Nothing was missing. cargo test 16 passed.

features.name: Bottom-anchored transcript
features.description: render::transcript_window(total, height, scroll_up) returns (blank rows above, first line, one past last). A transcript shorter than the viewport now pads ABOVE instead of below, so the first message sits just over the input like a shell prompt rather than stranded at row 0 with a screen of empty space under it. scroll_up is also clamped so it cannot walk past the first line.
features.evidence: Reported from a screenshot: the first reply rendered at the top with a large gap above the input. tui::tests::transcript_sits_on_the_input_instead_of_floating_at_the_top covers empty, short, exactly-full, overflowing, scrolled, over-scrolled, short-plus-scroll and zero-height. cargo test 18 passed. Needs a visual confirm in a live TUI.

features.name: Type-to-filter in the pickers
features.description: Pick gained a `filter` string and a visible() that keeps rows whose label contains it, case-insensitively — so /model (37 profiles), /resume and /tree all narrow as you type. idx/top reset on every keystroke, Backspace deletes, Enter on an empty result set does nothing, and the header shows '(3/37)  qwen▌'. The key guard now lets Ctrl+key fall through, so Ctrl+C quits instead of typing a 'c' into the filter, and a first Ctrl+C also closes the picker.
features.evidence: tui::tests::picker_filter_matches_anywhere_in_the_row_ignoring_case covers empty/hit/case-insensitive/substring-of-the-model-id/no-match. cargo test 18 passed. Needs a live TUI to confirm the keystrokes.
decisions: Substring, not fuzzy: the labels are short and a fuzzy matcher is either a dependency or a scoring function nobody asked for. Matching the whole label means 'zai-org' finds glm-5.1 by its model id, not just its profile name.

features.name: Permission answer stops being a message turn
features.description: Answering a permission prompt or an ask_user question used to do msg_num += 1 and push '2› y', so the reply was numbered as if it were the user's next message in the conversation — it is not; it never enters the session. App now records ask_line when the question is drawn, and close_ask() rewrites that line in place as 'ℹ <question> → <answer>', the same replace-in-place pattern ToolEnd uses for ToolStart. Esc and Ctrl+C route through the same helper, so an interrupted question is marked '→ interrupted' instead of being left hanging.
features.evidence: Reported from a live run: answering 'allow run_command pwd?' rendered as message 2. cargo test 19 passed; --self-test OK. Needs a live TUI to confirm the rendering.
decisions: Rewrite the question's line rather than append a second one: the answer belongs to the question, and one line keeps a long permission dialogue from doubling the transcript.

features.name: Shift+Enter inserts a newline
features.description: Enter with SHIFT or ALT inserts '\n' at the cursor instead of submitting (ALT because some terminals don't report Shift+Enter). The input box is now as tall as the draft: render::input_rows() renders one row per line with continuation rows aligned under the '> ', bottom_rows accounts for the height, and caret_at() puts the terminal cursor in the row that owns it. Up/Down walk the draft's lines while it is multi-line instead of recalling history, which would have discarded it.
features.evidence: tui::tests::shift_enter_drafts_move_the_cursor_by_line_not_through_history covers caret_at at line starts, ends and the last position, and move_line for column keeping, short-line clamping and both edges. cargo test 19 passed; --self-test OK. Needs a live TUI to confirm the terminal reports Shift+Enter at all.
decisions: Up/Down were rebound for multi-line drafts only. Leaving them on history would have made the first Up silently replace a half-written multi-line message.

features.name: Resumed transcripts replay tool lines
features.description: render_history() dropped every tool entry, so resuming a session showed the question and the answer with nothing in between — a turn that ran four tools looked like the agent did nothing. It now walks the assistant entry's tool_calls, builds each summary with the same ai_core::tool_summary the live path uses, and pairs them in order with the tool results chained after it (feat-026 guarantees that order). Entry gained `ok: Option<bool>`, set when the result is stored, so the replay draws the real ✓/✗; entries written before the field render a neutral '·'. The blank line after assistant prose is now only emitted when the turn actually ended there.
features.evidence: Diagnosed from the user's session.json: 7 entries — system, user 'hi', one assistant with four tool_calls, four tool results — of which only the two prose lines were rendered. tui::tests::render_history_replays_prose_and_tool_lines_but_not_the_system_prompt asserts the full line list including ✓/✗ pairing in call order, and a second session covers the neutral '·' for entries lacking `ok`. cargo test 19 passed. The binary could not be relinked (the user's TUI held it), so this is unconfirmed in a live resume.
decisions: Stored `ok` rather than guessing the outcome from the result text: 'user denied …' and 'error …' are heuristics that would mislabel a tool whose legitimate output mentions an error.
Durations are not replayed. They were never stored, and a wall time from a previous run is noise in a resumed transcript.

features.name: Session bookkeeping is status, not transcript
features.description: Event::Notice carries transient confirmations — resumed, branched at, exported to, renamed, plan mode on/off — to App.notice with a timestamp. The status line shows them for 3s and the 50ms render loop then stops drawing them, so nothing has to clear state. They no longer take a transcript line. Failures still go to the transcript, since a message you must read cannot vanish on a timer. Plain and CLI modes print notices normally.
features.evidence: Reported: 'resumed session.json (7 entries…)' sat in the chat. Confirmed removed from the transcript by dumping render_history against the real session.json — the replay contains only the user line, the assistant prose and four tool lines. cargo test 19 passed.

features.name: Release build under 15s and 43% smaller
features.description: /reload rebuilds with the release profile, so its build time is felt in the TUI. Keeping full LTO and codegen-units=1 (the size-optimal pair), the win came from opt-level="z" plus dropping reqwest's unused http2 and charset features: fat LTO's cost scales with how much IR it merges, so less code helps both time and size. 23.5s/3.27MB -> 13.7s/1.87MB. The full measurement table lives in Cargo.toml.
features.evidence: Measured each profile warm then timed after `touch src/main.rs`; the first build after any profile or dependency change recompiles the world and was discarded (16.2s vs a 13.6/13.7/13.8s steady state over three runs). opt-level 3/2/s/z = 23.5/24.0/19.0/15.7s. incremental=true measured, no effect. Re-verified after the feature trim: TLS handshake to https://example.com (HTTP 405 back), live streaming + a tool call against the local proxy, and web_fetch over https. cargo test 19 passed; --self-test OK on the release binary.
decisions: Kept lto=true and codegen-units=1 as the user asked, and found the time elsewhere — opt-level="z" is both cheaper to optimize and smaller than the default 3.
Dropped reqwest default features (http2, charset): HTTP/1.1 is universal and .text() assumes UTF-8, which every page we would fetch uses. Verified TLS and streaming still work rather than assuming.

features.name: Retries count on one line
features.description: Event::Retry { attempt, of, wait_ms, err } replaces the plain text line the retry path used to emit. attempt == 1 pushes a new row and later attempts rewrite it, so three retries are one counting line instead of three near-identical ones. Because attempt == 1 always starts fresh, no state needs clearing between turns. Piped and CLI output still prints one line per attempt — there is nothing to rewrite in a pipe.
features.evidence: Plain path verified live against the dead :8080 endpoint: three attempts at 1.0s/2.0s/4.0s then the error. --self-test still exercises the 503 retry. cargo test 19 passed. The in-place rewrite itself needs a live TUI.

features.name: Release build 4.2s via thin LTO at cgu=4
features.description: feat-049 landed on thin LTO once and was reverted to protect binary size. User asked for under 10s, so the full lto x codegen-units matrix was measured: fat = 12.8s/1.87MB (cgu=1), 11.7s/1.97MB (cgu=4), 12.1s/2.02MB (cgu=16); thin = 6.9s/2.02MB, 4.2s/2.16MB, 4.1s/2.28MB. Fat cannot reach 10s at ANY codegen-units because it merges the whole program into one module and optimizes that serially - cgu only splits front-end codegen. Settled on thin + cgu=4: 12.8s -> 4.2s for 290KB.
features.evidence: Each profile warmed with a full build, then timed after `touch src/tui/render.rs`; six configurations measured. cgu=1 under thin LTO cost 2.7s of the 6.9s - thin optimizes units in parallel and a one-line edit recompiles the one large rusti crate, so a single unit serialized the dominant work. fat/cgu=16 is strictly dominated: same 2.02MB as thin/cgu=1 for 5s more. cargo test 21 passed; release binary --help OK.
decisions: Reversed the feat-049 decision to keep fat LTO, but only after showing fat's floor is 11.7s - the earlier 'keep fat, find time elsewhere' option no longer exists under a 10s target.
panic="abort" left OFF despite the time it would save: tools.rs joins reader threads with join().unwrap_or_default() to survive a panicked reader, and abort turns that into a dead TUI.

features.name: Picker filter types at the prompt; user and tool lines get distinct weight
features.description: Typed picker filter rendered in the picker header next to the row count instead of at the input line. Now the filter IS the draft while a picker is open, shown at the > prompt with the block cursor; the real draft is hidden until Esc. Separately, transcript weight was flat: user queries, model prose and tool output all drew at full brightness. User lines now carry a cyan N-caret marker with bright text, tool output is 256-colour 245, and the status line moved from right-aligned to left.
features.evidence: colorize_row output captured byte-for-byte and checked: user = ESC[36m7>ESC[0m + bright, tool = coloured glyph + ESC[38;5;245m, thinking = ESC[3;38;5;249m, stats = ESC[2m. cargo test 21 passed.
decisions: Split user lines out of style b'k' into b'u'. They shared a style with tool rows, so dimming the tool fallthrough would have dimmed every WRAPPED row of a long query while its first row stayed bright. A test wraps an 80-column query to pin this.
Used 256-colour 245 rather than ESC[2m for tool text, for the reason already recorded on THINK: Windows Terminal renders ESC[2m as barely-darker.

features.name: /settings toggles status-line segments; context % always shown
features.description: ctx% existed in footer_right but was gated on ctx > 0, and turn_ctx resets to 0 at the start of every turn - so the reading vanished exactly while you were watching it fill. Gate removed. Added /settings, which reuses the existing picker with a new PickKind::Settings whose Enter toggles instead of closing, persisting to model.json via the existing Config.
features.evidence: Round-trip test writes a model.json with default/models/allow and no footer key, confirms it loads all-on, flips one segment, saves, and reloads with the other keys intact. Tests also pin that plan mode survives every segment being off. cargo test 21 passed.
decisions: Plan mode is deliberately NOT toggleable: it is the reason writes get refused, so hiding it would hide why.
Reused the picker instead of adding a menu system; the only behavioural difference is that Enter does not close, since you usually flip more than one row.
Dropped the on-marker from settings rows - the picker already draws a cursor caret, so a second caret for 'enabled' read as two cursors.

features.name: Running tools show a turning spinner in bold
features.description: ToolStart wrote a LITERAL braille frame, so a running command looked identical to a stalled one, and its text was dim - the same weight as finished output. The live spinner frame is now substituted at draw time from app.spinner (which already ticks every 50ms for the status line) and the running row is bold. ToolEnd's swap to the check/cross glyph is what un-bolds it.
features.evidence: Test asserts a running row renders the PASSED spinner frame (not the stored one) and is bold-and-not-dim, while a finished row is dim-and-not-bold. cargo test 21 passed. The animation itself needs a live TUI.
decisions: Substituted at render time rather than storing the animation: storing it would mean rewriting app.lines every 50ms tick just to move one character, which fights the differential renderer.

features.name: MCP client with per-server on/off
features.description: Tier-3c backlog item. stdio transport, JSON-RPC 2.0, written directly against std::process and serde_json - no MCP SDK and no new dependency. Servers are declared in model.json under "mcp" (command, args, env, enabled); enabled ones are spawned before the first frame, handshaken (initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/list), and their tools merged into tool_schemas() as mcp__<server>__<tool>. dispatch() routes by prefix rather than gaining an arm per server. /mcp lists servers with live state and toggles them, connecting or killing on the spot and persisting the choice.
features.evidence: Verified three ways. (1) tests/fake_mcp_server.py - a real stdio server - proves the wire format end to end: tools/list, tools/call, isError, and an unknown name refused client-side. (2) The same test exercises the Windows cmd /C path, since cfg!(windows) is true on this machine. (3) Ran the real npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything through the actual Rust client: 13 tools discovered, mcp__everything__echo called, 'Echo: hello from rusti' returned. cargo test 24 passed.
decisions: MCP tools are ALWAYS permission-gated and always plan-blocked. GATED is a fixed list of built-ins; a third-party tool's effects cannot be read off its name, so gated() treats every MCP tool as mutating even when it only reads. This is the one place the feature is deliberately not lazy.
Advertised name is stored beside the original rather than parsed back off at call time: slug() is lossy ('a.b' and 'a_b' both become 'a_b'), so reversing the prefix would mis-route.
On Windows the command goes through cmd /C: npx/uvx are .cmd shims and CreateProcess cannot run them directly - the single most common reason MCP servers 'are not found' on Windows.

Reader THREADS per pipe, not blocking reads: recv_timeout can give up on a hung server, a blocking pipe read cannot. stderr is drained (not nulled) both to keep a full pipe buffer from looking like a hang, and so a failure can report why.
Tools whose prefixed name exceeds 64 chars are dropped with a warning - the OpenAI-compatible API rejects the whole request otherwise, which would break every tool, not just the long one.
BTreeMap for the server map so the tool list order is stable across runs and stays prompt-cacheable.

features.name: A malformed model.json is reported, and never overwritten
features.description: Config::load_from collapsed three outcomes into one: no file, unreadable file, and unparseable file all returned Config::default() with both errors dropped by .ok(). Since /settings and /mcp do load -> flip -> save, a single typo in model.json silently became an empty config AND was then overwritten with those defaults on the next toggle, taking models, the allow list and the MCP server block with it. load_from now returns the defaults only for a genuinely missing file; an existing file that will not read or parse keeps the defaults so the process still runs but records the reason in Config.err (serde(skip)), and save_to refuses while err is set. The warning is surfaced on stderr for the one-shot and --list/--use paths, and pushed into the TUI transcript because stderr is invisible under the alternate screen.
features.evidence: cargo test 25 passed (new: config::tests::a_malformed_file_is_reported_and_never_overwritten, which asserts err is set, that save_to errors, that the file is byte-identical afterwards, and that a missing file still saves normally). Live against a real malformed model.json: --list prints the serde message with line/column then the usual empty-model line; --use exits 1 without writing; the one-shot path prints the warning and runs on defaults; the file was byte-identical in every case.
decisions: One choke point in save_to rather than a guard at each of the three call sites (/settings, /mcp, --use/--add): every present and future writer is covered by the same check.
Config.err is serde(skip) so the flag never round-trips into the file it describes.
A missing file stays a silent first run - that is the normal bootstrap path, not an error.
An existing file that fails to read for any other reason (permissions, lock) is treated exactly like a parse failure; only ErrorKind::NotFound means first run.
The TUI puts the warning in the transcript, not the 3s status-line notice: a warning you must act on must not expire.

features.name: A panic restores the terminal instead of wrecking it
features.description: The TUI enabled raw mode and entered the alternate screen, then undid both with two plain sequential calls after ui_loop returned. A panic unwinds straight past them, so the shell was left with no echo, no prompt and no line editing, on a buffer that discards the panic message on the way out. The restore is now restore_terminal(), shared by the normal exit and by a panic hook installed just before raw mode is enabled. The hook restores first and then delegates to the previous hook, so the message prints on the primary buffer where it can actually be read.
features.evidence: cargo test 26 passed (new: tui::tests::only_the_ui_thread_restores_the_terminal, which asserts the predicate is false on a worker thread - the case the test harness itself provides - and true on a thread named main). --self-test OK, cargo clippy clean, release build 4.3s. The restore sequences themselves are the same two calls the normal exit has always used, now shared rather than duplicated.
decisions: The hook is gated on the UI thread (name() == Some("main")): every worker here is an unnamed thread::spawn, and a panicking worker restoring the terminal would tear the screen down while the TUI is still rendering on it - worse than the panic it is reporting.
Restore runs BEFORE the previous hook, not after: the panic message must land on the primary buffer, not on the alternate screen that is about to be discarded.
Installed inside the is_terminal branch only, so the piped/plain path keeps the default hook.
restore_terminal() is idempotent - leaving an alternate screen you are not on and disabling raw mode that is off are both no-ops - so the hook firing after a normal exit is harmless.
Still not turning on panic="abort": tools.rs and mcp.rs join reader threads and rely on unwinding, and this was the reason that setting was listed as blocked in feat-051.

features.name: /reload builds in the warm target dir instead of a 1.1GB private one
features.description: /reload passed --target-dir target/reload, a second full build tree that never shared an artifact with ordinary cargo builds: 1.1GB on disk, and the first reload after any profile or dependency change paid a cold rebuild of every dependency instead of feat-051s 4.2s. The private tree existed for one reason - cargo uplifts the binary to target/release/rusti, and that file is usually the running process, which cannot be overwritten (Windows locks a running exe, Unix returns ETXTBSY). Renaming a running binary is allowed on both, so free_the_output_path() moves it aside before the build and /reload now builds in MANIFEST_DIR/target like everything else.
features.evidence: Mechanism proved on this platform with a live process: overwriting the running exe failed with Device or resource busy (the premise of the old design), renaming it succeeded. Whole sequence then simulated against the real tree with the exe running - move aside, cargo build --release, 4.32s with one crate recompiled rather than a cold rebuild, binary re-uplifted, staged copy ran and printed rusti 0.1.0. Separately confirmed cargo re-links a missing-but-fresh uplift in 0.11s, so moving the file aside never forces a rebuild. cargo test 27 passed (new: tui::tests::same_file_needs_both_paths_to_exist), --self-test OK.
decisions: same_file() requires BOTH paths to canonicalize: the trap is that canonicalize() errors on a missing path, so treating (Err, Err) as equal would call any two non-existent paths the same file and move something aside that cargo was never going to write.

The moved-aside binary is named rusti-old-<ms> and lands in the target root, which is exactly where stage_reload_exe already sweeps rusti-* - so it is cleaned up by the existing sweep rather than by new code. In-use ones fail to delete and go on the next sweep.
No move when the process is already a staged copy (the 2nd and later reloads): cargo can overwrite target/release/rusti freely then.
target/reload is now dead and can be deleted by hand; not deleted from code, since a tool should not remove 1.1GB it did not create this run.

features.name: Ctrl+O reveals successful tool output
features.description: feat-031 showed the tail of failed tool output only, so a successful cargo test or grep left you watching a green tick that told you nothing. The output was thrown away at the emit site (output was set to an empty string when ok). It is now always carried, and the TUI pushes a successful tools tail into the transcript behind a HIDDEN marker prefix; Ctrl+O flips App.expand and the renderer draws those rows. render_history does the same for a resumed session, so the toggle works on replayed turns too. Failures are unchanged and always visible.
features.evidence: cargo test 28 passed, including a new render::tests::hidden_rows_appear_only_when_expanded (folded output omits hidden rows, expanded shows them with the marker stripped) and the feat-047 replay test updated to expect the carried tails. --self-test OK. Live on the piped path against mimo-v2.5-pro: a successful read_file still prints just its tick and no tail, confirming the pipe behaviour did not change now that output is always carried.
decisions: A marker prefix on the row (HIDDEN = U+0001) rather than a parallel Vec<bool> or a struct per line: app.lines is pushed to from a dozen places and two containers that must stay in step is the bug. Nothing else in the TUI has to know hidden rows exist.

One filter point - render::visible() - so tool_line/ask_line/retry_line indices into app.lines keep working untouched, and the marker is stripped before drawing so it can never reach the terminal as a control character.
Failures stay visible always: a message you must read cannot sit behind a keystroke. Same rule as feat-048 kept failures out of the 3s notice.
An entry whose ok was never recorded (older sessions) hides like a success: an unknown outcome is not a failure and does not get to push its tail on screen unasked.
The piped path still prints tails only on failure - a pipe has no keyboard to press Ctrl+O with.
Ctrl+O also sets a status-line notice, so the key confirms itself even when nothing on screen changes (no tool output yet).

features.name: Edits report +N -M on the tick row, with the hunk behind Ctrl+O
features.description: write_file, edit_file and multi_edit reported bytes and char counts, which say nothing about what changed - and /undo could put an edit back but you could not see it first. tools::diff_block() trims the lines two texts share at the head and tail and reports what is left as (removed, added, rows). multi_edit calls it per (old, new) pair, which is exact because the caller already knows each changed region; write_file calls it once on the file it is replacing. The counts go on the end of the result first line, where ai_core::edit_stat() reads them back so the TUI can put +N -M on the tick row; the -/+ rows ride in the result and so appear under Ctrl+O through feat-059.
features.evidence:
cargo test 30 passed (new: tools::tests::diff_block_reports_only_what_changed covering middle change, pure append, new file, no-change and the row cap; mcp::tests::edit_stat_only_matches_a_real_pair covering both-halves-or-nothing and digits-not-words). --self-test OK. Live with --yolo against mimo-v2.5-pro: an edit_file of one word rendered "✓ _difftest.txt  +1 -1" and stored "edited _difftest.txt: 1 edit(s) +1 -1
  · - beta
  · + BRAVO"; a write_file creating a new file rendered "✓ _difftest2.txt  +3 -0" with three + rows.
decisions: No LCS and no diff crate: multi_edit passes one (old, new) pair at a time, so its hunks are exact by construction, and write_file has a whole-file replacement where a single trimmed hunk is the honest shape. A real diff algorithm would buy nothing on either path.
The trim keeps at least one line per side (max_tail clamp): without it a pure append counts the shared tail as both head and tail and reports a change it cannot show.
Rows capped at DIFF_ROWS=8 plus an elision line, so one cap bounds both the tokens the model is charged for and the tail Ctrl+O renders.
The stat travels in the result string rather than a new Event field, so a resumed session gets it too - render_history reads it back off the stored entry with the same helper.
edit_stat requires both a +N and a -M of digits, so an unrelated result ending in two number-ish words cannot grow a fake stat on its row.
Dropped the old "{o} chars -> {n} chars" wording: lines changed is what the reader wants, and two counts saying almost the same thing is worse than one.

features.name: read_file reads images and attaches them for vision models
features.description: read_file was fs::read_to_string, so a .png failed with "stream did not contain valid UTF-8". It now detects png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp by extension, base64-encodes the bytes into a data: URL and parks it; the agent loop attaches it to the conversation as a user message with OpenAI content parts. Entry gained an optional image field (a data URL) and Entry::to_message emits [{type:text},{type:image_url}] when it is set. A hand-written 16-line base64 encoder rather than a dependency, 4 MB raw cap, and the attachment is appended after ALL tool results of a turn so it cannot orphan a tool call.
features.evidence: cargo test 33 passed - new: tools::tests::b64_matches_the_rfc_vectors (all RFC 4648 vectors plus high bytes), tools::tests::image_mime_is_extension_only_and_narrow, session::image_tests::an_image_entry_becomes_content_parts (including that a tool message stays a string). --self-test OK. Wire-level proof from the real binary: pointed rusti at a capturing HTTP endpoint and the request carried role user with content [text, image_url] holding the full data URL, positioned after the tool result, with the tool message still a plain string. The stored data URL also decodes byte-identical to the original PNG. NOT verified: a model actually describing the picture - the :20128 proxy strips image parts, confirmed independently of rusti by raw curl against three models, each answering that the image was omitted. NOW VERIFIED END TO END (2026-09-15): the proxy was the only thing in the way. 9router 0.4.80's openaiToCommandCode transform replaced every image part with the literal text [image omitted]; patched locally to emit a real image part. With that one change rusti read _bands.png (240x240, known bands 220,40,40 / 40,200,60 / 40,80,220) and the model named red, green, blue top to bottom - answering from pixels, with decoding forbidden in the prompt. Same result from raw curl and from pi, so the attach path is proven against a live vision model, not just at the wire.
decisions: The image travels on a user entry after the tool results, never on the tool message: an OpenAI tool message takes a string only. Appending it after ALL results of the turn keeps every tool_call paired with its result (feat-026).

Entry.image beside content rather than turning content into parts: export, replay, compaction and the tree all want the text, and only the request builder cares that a picture rides along. One optional field instead of a type change rippling through six files.
A static PENDING_IMAGE handoff from the tool to the agent loop, in the style of UNDO/JOBS, so dispatch keeps its (bool, String) signature for all 17 tools.
Hand-written base64: 16 lines against a new dependency, on a codebase that measures its build time.
4 MB raw cap. Base64 inflates by 4/3 and history is re-sent every turn, so a large screenshot is a recurring cost, not a one-off.

Under 1 KB the result says bytes, not KB. It first said "0 KB" for a 105-byte PNG, and the model read that as an empty attachment and refused to look at the picture it had been sent - what a tool says about its result is part of the interface.
Extension-only detection: sniffing magic bytes would send every binary the model asked for, and a .rs file must never take the base64 path.

features.name: Ctrl+V / Alt+V paste a clipboard image into the input
features.description: The TUI can now take a screenshot straight off the clipboard. Both chords call tools::clipboard_image(), which saves the clipboard bitmap to .rusti/clips/clip-<ms>.png and returns the path; the key handler types that path into the input at the cursor, and read_file attaches the image when the message is sent (feat-061). A file COPIED in a file manager is a file-drop list rather than an image, and that path is returned as-is with nothing written - it is how most people copy a screenshot. Clips older than a day are swept on each paste. Windows goes through powershell -NoProfile -Sta, macOS through osascript, Linux through xclip/wl-paste with png then bmp.
features.evidence: Verified live on this machine, both branches. Bitmap branch: a known 64x64 PNG was put on the clipboard with Clipboard::SetImage, clipboard_image() wrote .rusti/clips/clip-1789407051990.png, and decoding both confirmed 64x64 with identical pixels at top (200,30,90) and bottom (30,120,200) - GDI+ re-encodes as RGBA so the byte size differs while the image does not. File-drop branch: Clipboard::SetFileDropList with the same file returned D:CodeAIAgentsustypi_clip_src.png directly and wrote no clip at all. cargo test 34 passed, --self-test OK. The keystroke itself is unverifiable here - the TUI needs a tty - and Windows Terminal may swallow ctrl+v, which is why alt+v is bound as well.
decisions: Both chords, one function: Windows Terminal binds ctrl+v to its own text paste and usually never delivers the key, while alt+v always arrives (feat-046 already relies on ALT reaching the app). Claude Code makes the same split - alt+v on windows/wsl, ctrl+v elsewhere - found by reading the strings in its shipped binary.
One process, not the probe-then-save pair Claude Code uses: the save script already exits 1 when there is no image, which is the same answer for a third of the latency.
powershell -Sta, never pwsh: the clipboard needs a single-threaded apartment and pwsh is MTA, where GetImage() returns null on a machine whose clipboard is fine.

The path is typed into the input rather than an [Image #1] placeholder backed by a side table: read_file already attaches images, so the path IS the plumbing. The cost is one visible path and one tool round-trip.
Sweep clips older than a day, not all but the newest - two images pasted into one unsent message would otherwise delete each other.
A failed paste sets a status notice rather than doing nothing: a silent key reads as a broken key.
The live clipboard test is opt-in behind RUSTI_CLIPBOARD_TEST=1. It overwrites the clipboard, which no one wants from a routine cargo test, and a headless machine has none.

features.name: The turn stats line reads worked 4m 32s and done 11:03 PM
features.description: The per-turn row showed a bare 9.1s, which stops being readable the moment a turn runs past a minute, and nothing said WHEN it finished - so a turn you walked away from gave no way to tell how long ago it landed. The row leads with both times - "worked 4m 32s · done 11:03 PM" - and the token accounting follows. human_dur() prints tenths under a minute, m/s under an hour and h/m above it; clock() renders a 12-hour local finish time from a unix timestamp and an offset. std has no local time, so utc_offset_min() derives it once per process by diffing echo %TIME% (or date +%H:%M) against the same instant in UTC, snapped to a quarter hour.
features.evidence: cargo test 34 passed. New assertions cover human_dur across the three ranges and the exact boundaries, clock() at both ends of the 12-hour day plus offsets that wrap past midnight in either direction, and parse_hm against an AutoRun banner. Derivation checked against this machine: utc epoch %86400 = 17:37, cmd echo %TIME% = 23:07, diff 330 min, snapped 330 (+5:30), and clock() renders 11:07 PM - the real local time. --self-test OK.
decisions: No chrono or time crate for two format strings. One cheap spawn per PROCESS, cached in a OnceLock, then pure arithmetic on the time of day - no dates, so no month lengths or leap years to get wrong.
parse_hm takes the LAST non-empty line, not the whole output: a machine with a cmd AutoRun banner would otherwise parse junk, return offset 0, and silently print every finish time in UTC.

The offset snaps to 15 minutes because the two clocks are read milliseconds apart and the raw difference can be a minute off; quarter-hour granularity covers every real zone including the :30 and :45 ones.
ponytail: a session running across a DST change keeps the offset it started with. Named in the code, re-read per turn if anyone ever notices.
Seconds keep a decimal and minutes do not - at 4m 32s the tenths are noise, at 9.1s they are the interesting part.
The test matches the head of the row with starts_with: the finish time is wall-clock and cannot be asserted exactly without injecting a clock, which is more plumbing than the line is worth.
Row order: both times first, then tok/tps/ctx. The two questions after a turn are how long it took and when it landed; the accounting is what you read second.

features.name: The status line sits above the input, not under it
features.description: The frame was composed transcript, spacer, panel, input, status - so the working spinner, notices and the session footer were drawn on the very last row, below the box you type in. The status block is now pushed before the input, which makes the input the last block on screen and puts the status directly above it. The caret math moved with it: input_top is h - input_len rather than h - 1 - input_len, and the clamp is the last row rather than the second to last.
features.evidence: cargo test 34 passed, --self-test OK, release build clean. The composition itself is inside draw(), which needs a terminal, so the row order is confirmed by reading and by the user running the TUI - the caret clamp is the part that would misbehave first if it were wrong.
decisions: Status goes between the panel and the input, not above the panel: a picker and the input belong together at the bottom, and the status is what separates them from each other rather than from the transcript.
bottom_rows is unchanged at 2 + input + panel - the same two fixed rows, in the other order - so the transcript height and its bottom-resting pad (feat-043) need no adjustment.

features.name: A model that cannot see an attached image must say so
features.description: First real use of feat-061 produced a confident, invented description of a screenshot. session.json shows rusti did its part - two read_file calls, two user entries each carrying a 13198-char data URL - and the :20128 proxy stripped both, leaving the model with only the text note. It then described the picture from the filename and the surrounding conversation, and even reasoned from the KB figure in the note ("quite small (9 KB) so hard to read the details"), which is meaningless for pixels it never received. The attached entry now carries an explicit instruction to say so rather than guess, and the system prompt extends its no-inventing rule from file contents and command output to what an image shows.
features.evidence: Diagnosed from the live session file rather than guessed: 42 entries, 2 carrying image parts, both for that screenshot, each 13198 chars of data URL - so the attach worked and the provider dropped it. Matches the earlier raw-curl finding that this proxy strips image parts on three different models. cargo test 34 passed, --self-test OK. Then PROVEN live with the same screenshot: the model answered "I cannot actually see the contents of the image" and offered alternatives, where the identical question had previously produced an invented description of rusti's TUI. Its reasoning also exposed the provider marker - the proxy substitutes the literal text "[image omitted]" for the image part, which is the first direct evidence of where the picture is dropped.
decisions: The instruction rides on the attached user entry, not only in the system prompt: it is the message the picture is supposed to be in, so it is the message a model reads when the picture is missing.

The KB figure stays in the tool note. It was misused as evidence about content, but it is genuinely useful for spotting a truncated or empty file - the instruction is the fix, not removing information.
No attempt to detect provider support. Nothing in an OpenAI-compatible response says whether image parts survived, so the only honest lever is telling the model what to do when they did not.

The proxy substitutes "[image omitted]" text for the image part - found in the model's own reasoning during the guard test. That string is the provider's, not rusti's, and is the clearest proof yet that the request is accepted and the picture discarded downstream.

features.name: The mouse wheel scrolls the transcript instead of walking input history
features.description: Reported as "the scroll wheel goes to an earlier user message and I cannot scroll up through the session". Without mouse capture a terminal converts wheel movement into Up/Down key presses on the alternate screen, and this TUI binds Up/Down to input-history recall - so every wheel notch recalled an older message instead of scrolling. The TUI now enables mouse capture and maps ScrollUp/ScrollDown to the transcript scroll, 3 rows a notch. Separately, scroll_up was unbounded: PageUp added 10 forever while the renderer clamped what it drew, so after a few extra presses the view sat pinned at the top and every scroll back down was silently eaten until the count unwound. RenderState now records max_scroll each frame and both the wheel and PageUp clamp to it.
features.evidence: cargo test 34 passed, --self-test OK, release build clean. The wheel itself needs a terminal, so the user confirms; the two causes were identified from the code - Up/Down are bound to history recall at the key handler, and scroll_up had no upper bound at its only two call sites.
decisions: Mouse capture is the fix rather than treating Up/Down as scroll when the input is empty: the terminal stops synthesising arrows once an app captures the mouse, so the wheel and the keyboard stop fighting over the same event.
The cost is stated rather than worked around: with capture on, click-drag text selection needs Shift held in most terminals. That is the usual trade for wheel support and is one line to revert.
max_scroll lives on RenderState because only the renderer knows it - it depends on the wrapped row count and the terminal height, neither of which the key handler can see.
DisableMouseCapture goes in restore_terminal, so the panic hook (feat-057) undoes it too - a terminal left in mouse-reporting mode prints escape junk on every click.

features.name: The hint rides above the input, the session footer stays below it
features.description: feat-064 moved the whole status block above the input, which took the session footer (session, model, branch, ctx) up with it. The user wanted the two halves split: the spinner/notice/ctrl-c hint above the input where it sits next to the caret and is read while a turn runs, and session/model/branch/ctx pinned back on the last row where it is read at a glance. The single merged status row is now two rows - hint pushed before the input, footer pushed after it - so the hint no longer has to share a row and yield width to the footer.
features.evidence: cargo test 34 passed, --self-test OK on the freshly built binary (the running TUI held the exe, so it was moved aside first - the same lock free_the_output_path handles for /reload). Row order and the caret clamp are confirmed by reading, as draw() needs a terminal; the user confirms visually after /reload.
decisions: bottom_rows goes from 2 to 3 + input + panel: two pinned rows became three, so the transcript gives up exactly one row. Not free, and not worth hiding - the alternative was leaving the footer to share the hint's row, which is what the user asked to undo.
The caret math returns to feat-064's predecessor: input_top is h - 1 - input_len and the clamp is the second-to-last row, because the footer, not the input, now holds the last row.
The hint is left-aligned on its own row rather than right-aligned as it was when it shared with the footer: alone on a row, there is nothing to yield to.

features.name: The permission prompt is a chooser, not a line of text to type at
features.description: A gated tool asked with a flat transcript line - allow run_command git log? [y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (saved) - and waited for a typed letter, which reads as log output rather than as a question addressed to the user. Event::Ask now carries choices: a list of (label, answer). Empty means free text, which is what the ask_user tool still sends; non-empty opens the picker that /model and /resume already use, titled with the question and numbered 1. Yes / 2. No / 3. Yes, and stop asking for <tool>. The answer that travels back is the same string a typed answer was, so decide() and the plain front end are unchanged in behaviour.
features.evidence: cargo test 34 passed, --self-test OK, and the self-test now asserts decide() maps the exact strings the picker sends (yes/no/always), so renaming a row's value cannot quietly turn a yes into a denial. Panel layout is confirmed by reading; the user confirms visually.
decisions: Reused Pick rather than writing a prompt widget: the panel, its selection, its scroll window and its render path already existed, so the feature is a new PickKind and a few rows.

Esc answers 'no' instead of closing the panel. Every other picker can be dismissed because nothing waits on it; a permission question has a tool blocked on the reply, so a dismissable panel would hang the turn.
Digits 1-9 answer outright and letters do NOT filter. Filtering is right for 37 model profiles and wrong for three answers - typing 'y' would have hidden the very row it looks like it selects.

The choices ride on the event rather than the TUI sniffing the question text for '[y]es'. A front end that has to parse prose to know what kind of question it was received is a bug waiting for the wording to change.
Not built: Claude Code's 'Tab to amend', which edits the command before running it. That is a command editor, not a prompt, and nobody asked for it yet.

features.name: Edit hunks show red/green signs and real file line numbers
features.description: feat-060 already reported +N -M and put the hunk behind Ctrl+O, but every row rendered through the same dim '  · ' style as the turn stats, so a removed line and an added one looked identical, and neither said where in the file it was. line_style now reads the sign before falling through to stats, colouring the marker red or green while the code after it stays grey - the sign is what the eye needs, the code is context. diff_block takes a base line offset and numbers each row from base + shared-prefix, so the rows carry the file's own line numbers; write_file passes 0 and multi_edit passes the line where each fragment starts, read before the replacement moves it.
features.evidence: cargo test 35 passed (one new), --self-test OK. The render test asserts a '  · - ' row starts red, a '  · + ' row starts green, the code after the sign is still dim, and the '… N more changed lines' overflow row stays a plain stats row - that last one pins the arm ordering in line_style, which is the whole feature. The new tools test edits a real file twice and asserts the hunks say lines 2 and 5, so the base offset is verified against the filesystem rather than by reading.
decisions: Numbers come from a base offset passed in, not from searching inside diff_block: only the caller knows where the fragment sits, and multi_edit must read that position BEFORE replacen moves it.

For a sequence of edits the number is the line as of that edit - earlier edits in the same call have already shifted the file. That is the only numbering a sequential editor can honestly give, and it is what the model needs to place its next edit.
Sign coloured, code dim, rather than colouring the whole row: a hunk is context under a result line, and two fully-coloured blocks would outshout the answer.
Not done: interleaving removed and added lines pair by pair. That needs an LCS, and diff_block deliberately has none - the callers already know where the change is.

features.name: /themes: fifteen palettes, picked from a list and remembered
features.description: The colours were literals spread through render.rs - a cyan doing four different jobs and an ANSI blue 34 that is near-unreadable on a dark background. src/tui/theme.rs now holds a table of fifteen palettes (the ones drawn up in palette-samples.html: current, recommended, periwinkle, teal, violet, one-accent, solarized, gruvbox, nord, tokyo-night, catppuccin, high-contrast, colourblind, quiet, amber), each a struct of complete SGR sequences built by a macro from the bare codes. render.rs reads theme::current() instead of literals. /themes opens the picker with the list and each palette's note, /themes <name> switches outright, and the choice is saved to model.json so it outlives the process.
features.evidence: cargo test 36 passed (one new), --self-test OK, release build with no warnings. The theme test asserts every field of every theme is a well-formed SGR sequence, names are unique and typeable as an argument, and theme 0 is still 'current' - a hand-written table's failure mode is a typo, so that is what it checks.
decisions: Theme 0 is the palette that shipped before this feature, and the default stays there. An update that restyles everyone's terminal without being asked is the opposite of a theme feature.
The picker stays open on Enter, like /settings and /mcp: the whole screen is the preview, so walking the list IS the comparison. Esc closes.
The test checks index_of, not set(): set writes a global that the render tests read, and cargo runs tests in parallel, so flipping the theme mid-suite would make them flaky.
An unknown name in model.json keeps the default and says so in the transcript at startup, rather than being ignored - a theme that quietly does nothing is a bug report waiting to happen.
Stats rows moved from ESC[2m to the theme's dim grey. ESC[2m is barely darker in Windows Terminal, which is why THINK and DIM avoided it already; now every secondary row agrees.

features.name: Markdown tables render as columns, and fenced blocks are syntax-highlighted
features.description: A model that answers with a table printed raw pipes, and a fenced block was one flat tan. Tables: table_block() takes a run of lines as a block - a pipe row, a |---| separator, then pipe rows - because a column's width is the widest cell in it and cannot be known one line at a time; render_table() lays out aligned columns with the header in the theme's accent and a rule under it. Highlighting: one language-agnostic tokeniser marks quoted strings, a string used as a key (the colon after it is the tell), numbers, true/false/null and punctuation, leaving anything unrecognised in the block's own colour. New theme roles head/rule/key/string/num/boolean/punct derive from the palette a theme already has, so all fifteen got highlighting without new colour decisions; 'current' overrides the four syntax colours with Nord's, chosen off the sample sheet.
features.evidence: cargo test 38 passed (two new), --self-test OK, release build with no warnings. The table test asserts the separator row is what distinguishes a table from prose containing a pipe, that column 2 starts at the same offset in header and both body rows, and that a 26-column terminal truncates instead of multiplying rows. The highlight test asserts the key/string split (both quoted - the colon decides), that an escaped quote does not end a string, and that highlighting changes not one visible character. FIXED after live use (2026-09-15): the first real table showed two bugs the test had not covered. (1) The last row was drawn twice - once in the table, once as raw pipes - because the caller advanced by rows.len(), and the separator is consumed but is not a row; table_block now returns the consumed count with the rows, so the two cannot drift. (2) Cells kept their markdown: `index_repository` reached the screen with its backticks and the column was padded for characters that are never drawn. Cells now go through md_line before anything is measured. Both are pinned by the test.
decisions: A rule, not a box: the transcript is 2-space-indented plain rows, and box-drawing walls fight that. One ─ line under the header is what a terminal table needs.
Cells truncate, never wrap. A wrapped cell destroys the column alignment that is the entire reason for rendering the table rather than printing it.
When a table will not fit, the WIDEST column gives back width first - it is the one with slack, and shrinking every column equally would cut short cells that fit fine.
One tokeniser for every language, not a grammar per language. It only has to beat 'the whole block is one colour', and it marks what is unambiguous across C-likes, JSON, TOML and shell.
Syntax roles derive from the palette by default (key = accent, string = ok, number = code, boolean = info, punctuation = grey), so adding a theme stays one decision instead of seventeen.
The colours for 'current' were read off the screenshot's pixels rather than guessed: decoding it gave #88c0d0 and #a3be8c on #7b8496, which identified Nord exactly.

table_block returns (rows, consumed) rather than letting the caller derive it. The count is not rows.len() - the separator is eaten and is not a row - and deriving it at the call site is exactly what drew the last row twice.

features.name: Install with cargo install; settings live in ~/.rusti/config.json, project state stays in ./model.json
features.description: rusti read model.json from the cwd, so every new folder asked for a model again and API keys sat in each repo. Now Config::load merges two files: ~/.rusti/config.json (models, default, keys, theme, footer, mcp; RUSTI_HOME overrides the dir) and ./model.json (allow, max_iters, context). A top-level key the project file has overrides the global one and is saved back to the project; every other key saves to its home. The first run with an old model.json that has models and no global file moves the global keys home once. Install is `cargo install --path .`.
features.evidence: cargo test 39 passed (one new: global_and_project_files_split_and_merge covers migration, global-only save creating no model.json, a new allow landing in the project, a project override read and saved in the project with the global file byte-identical and still in force elsewhere, and a malformed global file freezing both files). --self-test OK with RUSTI_HOME pointed at a scratch dir. End to end on a copy of the real model.json: --list migrated all profiles to the test home, then --list in an empty folder showed them. The test found a real bug first: a project override of theme erased the global theme on save; save_pair now keeps the global value of any key the project overrides.
decisions: cargo install --path . is the installer. No script, no prebuilt binaries: anyone building rusti already has cargo. Add an installer when someone without a toolchain needs it.
allow stays per project: a tool answered [a]lways in one repo is not safe to auto-run in every repo.
Override is by whole top-level key, no deep merge. A project that sets mcp owns the whole map - the same thing a hand-edit reader would expect.

An old model.json keeps working without the migration (its keys are project-owned). The migration only runs when there is no global file yet, so it happens once and never fights a user's later project overrides.
No dirs crate: USERPROFILE/HOME is all it would read here. RUSTI_HOME exists so tests and --self-test never write the real ~/.rusti.
/reload needed no change: it builds from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR baked in at compile time, so an installed rusti in any folder still rebuilds its own source.
